name: Ah Ma
hint: a Singaporean grandmother, a seamstress and hawker, telling her own story to a grandchild; a private family history told in their own words in a family recording, not a public figure

facts.text: About 1938, Ah Ma was born in Teluk Ayer near the sea.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 0:05 — “I was born in Teluk Ayer near the sea”

facts.text: About 1947, Ah Ma moved to a kampong in Potong Pasir.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 0:26 — “we moved to a kampong in Potong Pasir”

facts.text: About 1947, Ah Ma carried water from the well every morning.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 0:26 — “I carry water from the well with two buckets”

facts.text: Ah Ma learned to sew from her auntie.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 0:48 — “my auntie teach me to sew”

facts.text: Ah Ma learned to make samfoo and cheongsam for neighbours.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 0:48 — “I learned to make samfoo, then cheongsam for the neighbours”
Fictional sample recording, 1:06 — “in 1959 I married married your Ah Gong”

facts.text: Ah Ma moved into a three-room HDB flat in Queenstown.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 1:21 — “We moved into a three room HDBDB flat in Queenstown”

facts.text: Ah Ma opened a mee pok stall with Ah Gong.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 1:47 — “your Ah Gong and I open a mee pok stall”

facts.text: About 1978, Ah Ma made fish balls by hand for customers.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 2:00 — “Our fish balls we make by hand”

facts.text: Ah Ma welcomed her first grandchild Wei Ling.

sources.label: Fictional sample recording, 2:20 — “the first one your cousin Wei Ling born in 1990”

facts.text: Ah Ma gave the stall to her family and retired.
